newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia reimposes import duty on heavy machines.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia reimposes import duty on heavy machines.

text.p: Malaysia has proposed reimposing import duty on heavy machinery, Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said in his 1997 Budget speech on Friday.

Among the machinery affected are mechanical shovels, tunnellers, boring or sinking machinery, tamping or compacting, scrapers, bulldozer or angledozer blade and parts of railway or tramway locomotives.
Currently, there are no import duties on the machinery, but the proposed reimpositions would range from five percent to 20 percent.
Anwar said that the reimposition of the duty was "a step to develop the local machinery and engineering industry." The reimposition is effective from Budget day.

He said that in the previous budget, activities involving repairs of heavy machinery had been classified as a promoted activity. This was to encourage small and medium industries to actively participate in reconditioning heavy machinery.
"However, efforts to recondition used heavy equipment is still unsatisfactory as a substantial number of such machinery remain abandoned and unused," the speech said.
